features.sectionTitle: Digital euros and dollars. The essentials, made simple.
features.sectionSubtitle: Send, exchange, and put money to work in onchain markets. Three jobs, one wallet.
features.f1Desc: Send digital euros or dollars to anyone, any day, in seconds. No bank hours, no borders.
features.f2Desc: Put your balance to work in open onchain markets like Aave, straight from your wallet. Your choice, every time.
features.f3Title: Dollars to euros. Euros to dollars.
features.f3Desc: Move between euros and dollars in a couple of taps, with the rate shown before you confirm.
features.noteText: Network fees and limits may apply. Exchanges run through independent providers under their terms. Market rates are set by third-party protocols, move with the market and are never guaranteed. This is not an investment product.

steps.title: Start in minutes. Stay in control.
steps.s1Desc: Sign up with your email. The wallet is yours from the first second, and only you control what’s in it.
steps.s2Desc: Receive EURC or USDC from anywhere, or top up straight from your bank.
steps.s3Desc: Send, exchange, or put your balance to work in onchain markets.
steps.noteText: Bank top-ups run through independent providers, where available, under their terms and identity checks. Network fees and limits may apply.

advantages.row1Subtext: EURC and USDC are digital euros and dollars issued by Circle, designed to hold their value one to one. Circle mints and redeems them and publishes what backs them.
advantages.bandBody: Your keys. Your wallet. Your money. Defied Money never holds your funds and never has your private keys. Every transaction happens from a wallet only you can export, and is recorded on the blockchain.
advantages.row1NoteText: Stablecoins are not bank deposits and are not covered by deposit guarantees. Read the issuer’s disclosures before you hold one.

safety.i1Desc: Your wallet key is created for you at sign-up and can be exported at any time. Defied Money never holds it. Anything the app automates for you, like covering network fees, runs under policies set on your wallet.
safety.i2Title: Sign in without a seed phrase
safety.i2Desc: Use your email or Google account. There is nothing to write down, photograph or lose.
safety.i3Title: Verification only where a bank needs it
safety.i3Desc: Holding, sending and exchanging need no identity check. Bank transfers and the card do, and those checks are run by the regulated providers behind them.
safety.i4Title: Money and markets you can inspect
safety.i4Desc: USDC and EURC are issued by Circle, which publishes its reserves. Onchain deposits go only to protocols with public, audited contracts.
safety.noteText: Digital assets and onchain protocols carry risk, and holdings are not covered by deposit guarantees.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.a1: Defied Money is a non-custodial wallet and software interface for supported onchain services. You can hold, send, receive and use supported stablecoins such as EURC and USDC from a wallet you control. Defied Money does not hold your assets, issue stablecoins or control the third-party protocols you may choose to use.
faq.a2: A stablecoin is a crypto-asset designed to reference the value of another asset, such as a fiat currency. EURC and USDC are designed to reference the euro and US dollar respectively. Defied Money is not their issuer and does not determine their reserves, redemption terms or regulatory status. Refer to the relevant issuer’s documentation and disclosures for details.
faq.a3: A non-custodial wallet is a wallet where you, rather than Defied Money, control access to the assets. Your wallet is created with your email and secured by cryptography. Defied Money does not hold customer assets or control the private keys used to access your wallet. You may be able to export your key to a compatible wallet, subject to the relevant wallet infrastructure and network functionality.
faq.a4: You control the assets in your self-custodial wallet. Defied Money does not hold customer assets or control the private keys used to access your wallet. Where supported by the relevant wallet infrastructure, you may export your key for use with a compatible wallet.
faq.q5: Can I withdraw at any time?
faq.a5: You can send supported stablecoins from your wallet when the relevant blockchain network is available. If you interact with a third-party protocol, its withdrawal or exit terms, liquidity and technical conditions determine whether and when you can withdraw. Review the protocol’s terms and risks before interacting.
faq.q6: Do I need to verify my identity?
faq.a6: Requirements may vary by feature and jurisdiction. Where available, fiat conversion between fiat currency and supported stablecoins is provided by independent third-party providers and may require identity verification under their terms and applicable law.
faq.a7: Digital assets and decentralised protocols involve risk, including loss of assets, smart-contract vulnerabilities, blockchain-network disruption, loss of wallet credentials, stablecoin issuer risk and regulatory changes. Third-party protocol rates are variable and returns are not guaranteed. Read our Risk Disclosure before using the service.
faq.q8: Are my funds covered by a deposit guarantee?
faq.a8: No. Stablecoins are not bank deposits, and holdings through a self-custodial wallet are not covered by national deposit guarantee schemes. Assets used with third-party protocols are also subject to their terms and risks.
faq.q9: What platforms does Defied Money support?
faq.a9: Defied Money is currently available as a web application, optimized for both desktop and mobile browsers. Native iOS and Android apps are in development.
faq.a10: EURC is a stablecoin designed to reference the value of the euro. Defied Money supports EURC but does not issue, mint, redeem or control it, and does not determine its reserves, redemption terms or regulatory status. Refer to the issuer’s documentation and disclosures for current information.
faq.q11: How is Defied Money different from traditional fintech apps?
faq.a11: Defied Money is designed as a non-custodial wallet and software interface. You control your wallet assets; Defied Money does not hold customer funds, issue supported stablecoins or operate the third-party protocols available through the interface. Features, availability and risks differ from those of traditional financial services.
faq.q12: Is Defied Money safe if I'm not an expert?
faq.a12: Defied Money is designed to make wallet use simpler, but self-custody has important responsibilities and risks. Protect your email, device and wallet credentials, and enable two-factor authentication. Defied Money cannot recover assets lost through compromised credentials or irreversible blockchain transactions.
faq.q13: Where do the rates come from?
faq.a13: Some third-party decentralised protocols display rates for particular onchain activities. These are current protocol rates, not rates offered or guaranteed by Defied Money. They can change at any time and involve smart-contract, liquidity, market and other risks.
faq.q14: Is Defied Money available in my country?
faq.a14: Availability and features may vary by jurisdiction and may be subject to eligibility, compliance, provider and technical requirements. Fiat conversion and card features, where available, are provided by independent third-party providers under their own terms.
faq.q15: What happens to my money if Defied Money shuts down?
faq.a15: Your assets remain in your self-custodial wallet. Access outside the Defied Money interface depends on the relevant wallet infrastructure, compatible wallet software and blockchain-network functionality. You should keep your credentials secure and understand the recovery options available to you.
